 Lakers complete wild comeback to beat Hornets behind Quentin Grimes’ 47 points, 10 3-pointers
 Quentin Grimes has absolutely popped off for the Lakers, making 10 threes and rescuing them at the death against the Hornets in regulation.
 By Jedd Pagaduan • Updated Nov 18, 2026 at 2:07 AM ET • 2 min read Add ClutchPoints on Google Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Where would the Los Angeles Lakers be without Quentin Grimes ? With Austin Reaves out due to a heel injury for their Tuesday night clash against the Charlotte Hornets, Grimes stepped into the starting lineup once more and has gone absolutely berserk — putting on a shooting clinic that will live long in Lakers fans' memories. And to top it all off, Grimes, with his 10th made three of the night, forced overtime after the Lakers had been fighting an uphill battle all game.
 Los Angeles was able to close the deal in overtime, finishing off a 118-114 win over the Hornets after trailing by as many as 18 points during the second half.
 The Hornets had an opportunity to ice the game at the foul line up by two with 12.1 seconds left in the game. Coby White would then split a pair, leaving the door open for the Lakers. Instead of taking a timeout, LA brought the ball up against a scrambling defense.
 It looked as though Luka Doncic was going to be the one to take the final shot. But he recognized Grimes' hot hand and dished it to him on a jumping pass. Grimes would then swish the ball through the net from beyond the arc, giving him his 10th triple on the night and 45 points in regulation — tying the game in the process and forcing overtime.
 QUENTIN GRIMES SENDS THE GAME TO OVERTIME WITH THIS WIDE OPEN THREE 🎯
 THIS IS HIS 10TH THREE OF THE GAME! pic.twitter.com/SG3GWfKsOH 
 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 18, 2026 
 Article Continues Below The Lakers would have suffered a blowout loss at home to the Hornets if Grimes weren't here. Instead, they get another win thanks to 47 points from Grimes and another 36 from Doncic.
 The Lakers fell behind the Hornets by as much as 18 points in what had been a frustrating night all around for the team. Head coach JJ Redick lost his cool at one point due to the purported disparity in officiating fairness.
 But in the end, it was Grimes who stepped up at exactly the right time for a Lakers team that needed a jolt of energy.
